scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 15 · KP01 The framework of cluster validity tests

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Data without groups: $k$-means still returns three clusters

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: both panels show the same $100$ points; the left is uncolored, the right is colored by $k$-means ($m=3$), and the black crosses are the three representatives.

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: $100$ points uniform in a square (no real groups)

scene-u01-pnew1-227.name: text#227
scene-u01-pnew1-227.text: Same points in both panels: the three clusters were imposed by the algorithm, not present in the data

scene-u01-pnew1-233.name: text#233
scene-u01-pnew1-233.text: Without clustering, ask whether $X$ has any clustering structure; see KP07.

scene-u01-pnew1-237.name: text#237
scene-u01-pnew1-237.text: Once structure is confirmed, assess the algorithm's output quantitatively.

scene-u01-pnew1-241.name: text#241
scene-u01-pnew1-241.text: "A tidy result means real groups were found." Wrong: tidiness only shows the algorithm did its job; the uniform data on the left are cut tidily too. Validity methods are tools for experts, not truth machines.

scene-u01-pnew1-243.name: text#243
scene-u01-pnew1-243.text: Demo data and numbers computed by code [Added]

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 15 · KP01 The framework of cluster validity tests

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Three things to compare a clustering $\mathcal{C}$ against

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: all three columns use the same four-group data ($25$ points each, standard deviation $0.06$); the bottom of each column says what it compares against.

scene-u01-pnew2-167.name: text#167
scene-u01-pnew2-167.text: Color: algorithm's $\mathcal{C}$; black rings: $P_2$, $P_4$ of the given $\mathcal{P}$

scene-u01-pnew2-168.name: text#168
scene-u01-pnew2-168.text: Assess $\mathcal{C}$ against an independent partition $\mathcal{P}$ that reflects your intuition

scene-u01-pnew2-314.name: text#314
scene-u01-pnew2-314.text: Proximity matrix $P$ ($3$ points per group, sorted by group): dark diagonal blocks mean close within groups

scene-u01-pnew2-315.name: text#315
scene-u01-pnew2-315.text: Use only quantities of $X$ itself, such as the proximity matrix

scene-u01-pnew2-341.name: text#341
scene-u01-pnew2-341.text: Compare with structures from other parameters or other algorithms

scene-u01-pnew2-342.name: text#342
scene-u01-pnew2-342.text: Ask: does it match my intuition?

scene-u01-pnew2-343.name: text#343
scene-u01-pnew2-343.text: Ask: does it fit the data itself?

scene-u01-pnew2-346.name: text#346
scene-u01-pnew2-346.text: Demo data and numbers computed by code [Added]

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 15 · KP01 The framework of cluster validity tests

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Validity test: the real $q$ must beat almost all random reference values

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the gray histogram is $\hat{\Gamma}_i$ of $100$ uniform data sets, the pink band is the right tail at $\rho=0.05$; the green and orange lines are $\hat{\Gamma}$ of two four-group data sets.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: $H_0$: the structure of $X$ is random; statistic $q=\hat{\Gamma}(P,Y)$

scene-u01-pnew3-35.name: text#35
scene-u01-pnew3-35.text: Right-tail rule: reject $H_0$ if $q$ exceeds $(1-\rho)r$ of the $q_i$; here $r=100$, so it must exceed $95$

scene-u01-pnew3-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew3-36.text: Rejecting a true $H_0$ is a Type $\mathrm{I}$ error, with probability $\rho$

scene-u01-pnew3-38.name: text#38
scene-u01-pnew3-38.text: Three hypotheses for the reference population

scene-u01-pnew3-42.name: text#42
scene-u01-pnew3-42.text: Ratio scale: drop $N$ points uniformly into a region such as a hypercube

scene-u01-pnew3-46.name: text#46
scene-u01-pnew3-46.text: Ordinal proximities only: fill ranks randomly into the upper triangle

scene-u01-pnew3-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew3-50.text: All labelings equally likely: tests an external partition

scene-u01-pnew3-51.name: text#51
scene-u01-pnew3-51.text: Generate $r$ reference sets, compute a $q_i$ for each, and approximate the distribution by a histogram.

steps.label: Algorithms impose structure
steps.speakerNotes: 100 uniform points: k-means (m=3) still returns clusters of 29, 34 and 37; so ask about clustering tendency first, then assess cluster validity.

steps.label: Three kinds of validity criteria
steps.speakerNotes: Same four-group data: external criteria compare with a given partition, internal criteria use only the proximity matrix, relative criteria vary m and compare J.

steps.label: The skeleton of a validity test
steps.speakerNotes: Γ̂ of 100 uniform reference sets lies in 0.567–0.693; tight groups (0.896) reject H0, loose groups (0.631) exceed only 74 and do not reject.
